Review Title: Unforgettable and MUST-DO flightseeing and Glacier Landing!
Review Text:
We took this tour last week while visiting Alaska, and included the Glacier Landing in our Denali Flightseeing Tour. Please trust me when I say you NEED to do the Glacier Landing!!! It is SO worth the extra money for the experience.

Booking Experience: Super easy and wonderful customer service. Unfortunately the weather was not cooperative and we had to rebook several times due to this. The ladies in the office were great to deal with and more than willing to refund if we couldn't get an alternate date (thankfully it worked for us another day!!). The day we were planned to go up, the weather started changing in the afternoon, and they got us up in the air about an hour early so that we could still do the Glacier Landing.

Pilot: Our Pilot for our flight was Jack and he was GREAT! Super friendly, funny and knowledgeable he made our experience a fun one. My son is 14 and wants to be a pilot someday. He got to sit in the Co-Pilot seat, so as you can imagine he was in his glory!! Jack did a great job of sharing history about Alaska, the mountains and the glaciers.

Glacier Landing: Again, you NEED to do this!! The landing and then taking back off were smooth. When you step out of the plane the complete SILENCE and STILLNESS are mind blowing! You feel like you're the only person in the world at that moment. It was a truly beautiful and mind-blowing experience. My son dropped down and did a snow angel in that perfectly undisturbed snow lol.

Flight: The flight was smooth and we were able to get SO many amazing pictures while in flight.

This is an adventure we will cherish and remember always. Thank you K2!!

Review Text: In all our research for Alaska, what stood out the most was the encouragement to see Alaska from as many perspectives as we could - land, sea, air. When we figured out that flightseeing out of Talkeetna would not only work great for our schedule, but allow us to experience the Alaska Range and Mount Denali, it wasn't a hard choice to go with K2 Aviation. The reviews were overwhelmingly positive, and we really appreciated the transparency on their website for the different routes available. From booking, to arrival, and check-in, the staff was very kind and helpful. I tend to be a bit of a nervous flyer ever since experiencing a super bumpy ride many years ago in a small 2 seater plane, but Lauren in the office was so encouraging and genuine in putting my mind at ease. We had booked the Denali Grand Tour, but due to weather conditions up there, we weren't going to be able to fly that route. Instead, we were offered the Denali Flyer and a refund for the price difference. For anyone wondering if a certain time of day is best, there really isn't, and all the staff confirmed this. Whatever time works best for you, is the best time to go! We were there for a 6:30 PM and it was an absolutely beautiful, sunny and clear day - and yet we still had changes because the cloud and/or wind conditions are always going to be completely different higher up and around the mountains. We had an absolutely fantastic time, and I felt great throughout the flight! I do recommend being on Dramamine or Bonine if you're prone to motion sickness and/or have some anxiety with flying - take one dose the night before to metabolize in your system, and one prior to your activity. Being prepared is key! Our pilot Mitch was very friendly, professional, and knowledgeable about anything and everything we saw from the air. The views were breathtaking, and we learned so much! It was an almost out of this world experience to feel like you're floating above and among the mountains. We were prepared to do a glacier landing, but some last minute cloud cover interfered. It was still an awesome experience though, and one we won't soon forget!

Review Title: Office lied to us consistently multiple times

I understand weather condition can change - the green tour may not be running in morning but might run at our scheduled time. Review Title: Incredible views of mountains (Denali) and glaciers
Review Text:
My family really wanted to go on a flight-seeing tour and land on a glacier, so we started searching for them while in Anchorage. We found several great options, but ended up going with K2 Aviation since their availability best matched our schedule. We chose the Denali Flyer Tour because we wanted to see multiple sides of Denali but didn't think the Grand Denali was quite worth the added cost.

We arrived really early since the drive from Denali to Talkeetna took less time than we anticipated. We hung out in the parking lot and on the picnic benches in front of K2. They provide water, tea, etc.There was also WiFi for guests but it didn't work for me.

We checked in 30-45 minutes before our flight. Each person weights themselves with everything they're taking onto the plane. You can also borrow sunglasses at this time if you need. They have a great selection with all sorts of styles and sizes. We also got our overboots at this time.

About 10 minutes before our flight, the pilot called us over and gave us a safety briefing. Then, we got on the plane. He took volunteers for co-pilot and everyone else sat wherever they wanted. Every seat has a headset and a window. The headset is a bit uncomfortable since it really closes in on your ears and head.

The flight itself was incredible! We flew over the park and soared through the mountains. Our pilot pointed out all the major landmarks from the summits to glaciers. He didn't provide much information besides that, which was fine with me. He did a good job of showing Denali to both sides of the plane so everyone was able to get photos.

Near the end of the flight, we landed on Ruth Glacier. It was more like a field of snow than glacier ice, which was a little disappointing, but still a beautiful place. We had about 15 minutes on the glacier and then we got back on the plane and headed back.

Oh! One thing to note, it was rather hot when we were in Denali (highs of 75-80). It was also warm on the glacier and basically everyone wore short sleeves and jeans or shorts. No gloves, beanies, jackets, etc. were necessary.

Overall, I would recommend the flight to folks considering it. I wouldn't say it was the highlight of my trip, but it was definitely up there!

Review Title: Was Great Experience, but there was a BIG safety concern
Review Text:
We had booked "Denali Flyer Tour with Glacier Landing". Glacier landing was the best. And "Denali Flyer" was good enough in terms of the length and the time of the tour. I wouldn't opt for for the other 3 tours. This is good enough.

Our tour was scheduled to start at 3:00 pm. We were a family of 6. We did a checkin at 2:30 pm. Be there 30 mins prior to boarding. There is a restroom at the office, clean. If you forget to get your sun glasses, no worries, the staff there are helpful and you can borrow sun glasses, and return them after the flight. You get to borrow the boots kind that you wear on top of your shoes. So keep in mind, you don't need to bring your boots. Just the regular shoes that you are wearing for your entire trip is good enough. You pick your size from their storage box, wear them, meet the pilot when called around 15 mins prior to flying. The pilot walks you to the 10 seater plane and you get seated.

You wear your headset.
FEEDBACK:
1. MY HEADSET WAS NOT CONNECTED TO THE SOCKET. AFTER FEW MINTS I HAD TO FIGURE OUT
2. THE WORST PART WAS: I WAS SITTING NEXT TO THE ENTRY DOOR AND THE FLIGHT STARTS MOVING, AND I'M SHOCKED THE DOOR IS NOT CLOSED. I REMOVED MY SEAT BELT AND RAN TO THE PILOT AND TAPPED ON HIS SHOULDER AND TOLD HIM THE DOOR IS NOT CLOSED. HE STOPPED THE PLANE AND CAME AND CLOSED/LOCKED THE DOOR.

That was terrible terrible mistake of the pilot not having a checklist. Had I taken a minute or more to inform the pilot, maybe we all wouldn't have been in the plane to even tell. I as a passenger don't know how to close and lock that plane door, and for sure I don't want to do it myself and feel safe.

Then we go over the mountain, which was beautiful to see the snow tip from areal view. Then we land on a 4000 ft glacier surrounded by snow mountains. It was "nature at it's best".. just gorgeous. Absolute beauty. Amazing. We get to spend more than 20 mins and then fly back. The pilot was a good narrator. We land back. Return our sun glasses, boots, and back to our car.

Oh, Talkeetna was cute little town, we had Ice Cream and coffee. Should try it. It was great. And there are lot of Thai Restaurants if that's a point to keep in mind

Review Title: Beautiful, Comfortable, Fun, We Would Do It Again!
Review Text: My wife and I did this air tour and thoroughly enjoyed it.  In addition to the pilot, Randy, there were three others on the flight.  We flew in a very well maintained 1958 deHavilland Beaver which alone is worth the trip, but we also saw the beauty of Dinali and the glaciers from the air.  As described, each person has a headset so that they can hear the description offered by the pilot and so that they can ask questions.  K2 picked us up at our hotel at the designated time and returned us after the flight.  We had a fairly good day weather-wise and were able to take a lot of beautiful pictures; the flight itself was very relaxing with little to zero turbulence (this is weather dependent I suppose), and the pilot/guide was very informative.  We would certainly do this again in the future and recommend it to others.

Review Text:
Our flight was postponed due to iffy weather but better to be safe than sorry and as it turned out the following morning was GORGEOUS for flying.

Our pilot had four decades of experience and handled the plane so perfectly that there was zero turbulence and we could simply sit back and enjoy the experience.

I actually didn't sit back because I had the seat beside the pilot, but also, I felt like a little girl flying over a magical land of glittery diamonds because the sun was reflecting off the snow on Dinali (and all around the mountain)…it literally took my breath away because I held my breath the whole time, not from nerves, but from sheer bewilderment at the beauty ahead and below me.

We landed on Ruth Glacier and had time to take photos, and just BE in all that natural beauty.

Flying back to base, we flew over more of the glacier and saw the turquoise ice through the snow, soooooo beautiful.

Sadly, we're damaging the environment so badly, that they say within 50 years what I saw could be gone....so if you have the opportunity to experience this, DO IT! It was worth every penny and one of the best experiences of my life.

P.S. I'm a senior travel consultant with 30 years in the business, and have (been blessed to have) had MANY amazing experiences during my travels, so when I say that the flight-seeing to Denali was a highlight, believe it.

I took SO many photos and videos, these are just a few of them.

Review Text: Wow.  Where do I begin. The meticulously clean DeHaviland DHC-3 Otter was our bird and Chris was our pilot.  My husband and I were two of only three passengers on the plane, and the mountain peaks, the craggy cliffs we saw  and the glacier we landed on (Pika Glacier) -- Everything Was So Incredible!!   What was super special was that Chris would explain everything he knew about what we were seeing (and he knows a LOT!).  All of it was so interesting -- we both want to return for another flight in the spring or summer when the snow in the lower elevations has melted and the green has "returned" -- and we will ask for Chris to take us on yet another flight.  He's a great guy who is meticulous with everything (EVERYthing) he does, and we want more of his stories!!  Thanks, K2, for the amazing experience (I still think you should have a "Frequent Flyer" card... 6 flights and the 7th is free... or something like that.  I'd be game!).

Review Text:
Wow! What an amazing experience this was. My two friends and I decided to book this flight tour (based on reviews here) during our after-season trip to Alaska. We assumed it would be cool, but it exceeded our expectations. Our pilot, Ryan, was knowledgable and friendly, and the plane was a cool Vietnam era craft (called an Otter, I think).

The weather for our tour was out of this world--totally clear sky and no clouds to be seen. They told us it was the best flying day they had seen in months! Getting to see Denali and the other peaks up close was breathtaking, and Ryan told us a lot of history and answered all of our questions expertly.

Denali was obviously the main attraction, but there were a lot of other beautiful peaks in the range, as well as some glaciers. It was fun to loop through the peaks and see so much.

I'm sure the tour would still have been great even if the weather wasn't so good, so I highly recommend this tour. Definitely book in advance. Also, volunteer for the copilot seat if they ask!

Review Title: Stunning bird's eye view of the and the mountains
Review Text:
Our final stop before driving back to Anchorage from Fairbanks was the Denali Flight tour with Glacier Landing with K2 Aviation. We had checked off everything on our Alaska trip except the flight + glacier landing and we are so glad that we flew with K2 aviation. The overall experience was just brilliant and one to savor for years to come.

The winds were rough near Mt Denali, so with some potential turbulence our Denali Grand tour was not possible but we were able to do the Denali Flyer. Our captain Mike with decades of experience was very nice to give us all the information about the Ruth glaciers and others. We got a good glimpse of Mt Denali from about 5 miles. The weather was so good when we landed on the glacier, we didnt even use our jackets. The view of all the other mountains was excellent and the glaciers especially was unreal. The formation, the journey and the final integration into the rivers of these glaciers was so exciting to see and fathom.

I would recommend everyone to try this out with K2 aviation and rest assured you wont be disappointed. The staff is very friendly and flexible at K2 and please do get your Alaska Tour saver coupon book for a flat 20% discount !

Next time it'll be the Grand tour / summit tour !

Review Text:

The planes were very clean and well maintained, very powerful and ideal for the type of work expected of them to fly in mountain terrain. Windows were very clean enabling surprisingly good photography.
The history of the area was well explained as we flew. Although we did not manage a glacial landing due to cloud conditions, the whole experience was exceptional.It would be one of the best experiences we had in our 3 weeks in Alaska. April, often seen as not a good time to be in Alaska due to the melting snow, actually was really good as the day light hours are long, the landscape is still well covered in snow, the lakes and rivers are largely still iced over, but thawing and there were no mosquitos yet to worry about!
Great experience and very much recommend.
